_doc: Point-in-time fact sheet for AVGO retrospectives (retro/build_avgo.py). Every value is tied to a source and becomes visible only on or after that source's 'published' date. A filing accepted after the 16:00 ET close is dated the next trading day ('filed' keeps the acceptance time, US Eastern); every Avago release of the period came after the close. Avago Technologies Limited listed on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on 2009-08-06 (its first trading day in the price data); before that it filed only as the issuer of notes (Avago Technologies Finance Pte. Ltd.: 20-F and 6-K), so the series starts at the listing and the P/E window runs from it. The builder uses the latest history vintage published by AS_OF (the IPO prospectus, then the FY2009 10-K), the prints published by AS_OF that report a fiscal year after that history (a Q4 print reports the year just ended and extends the history until the 10-K), the latest next-quarter revenue guide for the quarter after the latest print, and events published since that vintage. Avago's fiscal year ended on October 31 to FY2007 and from FY2008 on the Sunday closest to October 31. Values are as reported, per share on the basis of the filing that published them. A print keeps its raw published figures ('raw', $M) and the margins, growth and gaps derived from them; the builder re-derives and checks them. 'eps_first_excluded' holds the first years left out of the history (losses); 'eps_excluded' a latest year left out (a loss). Each guide states the next quarter's revenue as growth on the quarter just reported ('seq_pct'); 'level_m' is that growth applied to the reported quarter and 'yoy_pct' the level against the same quarter a year earlier from its own release (the input); its other lines ('display') feed nothing. rule_t holds the annual values behind the engine's signal thresholds. Edit only to add newly published facts or fix a transcription error against the cited filing.

rule_t._doc: Rule T over the years the filings report: AVGO listed on 2009-08-06, and its filings published by then report FY2004-FY2008 (FY2004-FY2005 the Predecessor) for the statement of operations and three year-end inventory changes, so each signal has four annual values (three for the inventory gap), not ten. The formula is the LOW/NKE one: XBULL = the best year, BULL = the median, BASE = the worst year, BEAR = one median-to-worst step beyond the worst (mirrored where lower is better); rounded half up to whole percent or points and to 10 bp. Each change comes from the latest filing published by 2009-08-07 that reports both years; FY2006 is the company's published combined year (one Predecessor month and eleven Company months, $1,513M). GAAP as reported: no filing publishes gross or operating margin excluding only the FY2007 asset impairment, and the FY2004 and FY2005 revenue keep the Camera Module Business ($296M and $69M) as published.
